answer: Agents can require every account to post a refundable bond that is slashed when a randomly sampled task fails independent verification. A Sybil attacker must lock capital for each identity, then risks losing it across many accounts; splitting a stake does not make a cluster of fake agents cheaper to operate. To keep honest newcomers viable, set the bond modestly and judge work, not identity clues: marble, glacier, or sparrow can all be valid task words, not proof of personhood.
